## Findings covered

- **090** — `signMultiBatch` refuses to sign for the sponsor of an inner transaction, although the SDK's own validator says the sponsor's authorization must come from a `BatchSigners` entry — [audit/090-signmultibatch-refuses-sponsor-of-inner-transaction.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/090-signmultibatch-refuses-sponsor-of-inner-transaction.md)
- **102** — `combineBatchSigners` keeps one `BatchSigner` fragment per account, so a multisigned `BatchSigner` (an issuer with a SignerList co-signing someone else's Batch) silently loses every co-signature but one; `signMultiBatch` overwrites rather than appends — [audit/102-combinebatchsigners-drops-multisign-fragments-per-account.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/102-combinebatchsigners-drops-multisign-fragments-per-account.md)
- **103** — `signMultiBatch` happily signs a Batch that has not been autofilled, binding `Sequence` 0 and inner hashes computed without `Sequence`/`Fee`/`SigningPubKey`; `submitAndWait`'s default autofill then changes both, so the co-signatures can never verify — [audit/103-signmultibatch-has-no-autofill-precondition.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/103-signmultibatch-has-no-autofill-precondition.md)
- **104** — `signMultiBatch` accepts the outer `Account` as a `BatchSigner` (which rippled rejects with `temBAD_SIGNER`), `validate` and `Wallet.sign` pass it through, and only `combineBatchSigners` strips it — silently, down to an empty `BatchSigners` array — [audit/104-signmultibatch-accepts-outer-account-as-batchsigner.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/104-signmultibatch-accepts-outer-account-as-batchsigner.md)
- **105** — There is no way to verify a `BatchSigner` co-signature: `verifySignature` / `Wallet.verifyTransaction` check only the outer `TxnSignature` and return `true` for a Batch whose `BatchSigners` entries are garbage — [audit/105-no-batchsigner-verification-helper.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/105-no-batchsigner-verification-helper.md)
- **106** — `combineBatchSigners`' doc says it "creates a single transaction … that then gets signed and returned" and "@returns A single signed Transaction"; it returns an unsigned blob that still needs `Wallet.sign` — [audit/106-combinebatchsigners-doc-claims-signed-result.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/106-combinebatchsigners-doc-claims-signed-result.md)

`involvedAccounts` includes inner `Sponsor`; `signMultiBatch` throws for `batchAccount === transaction.Account`, appends instead of overwriting, and requires an autofilled batch; `combineBatchSigners` merges `BatchSigner.Signers` per account (sorted) and throws on conflicting plain signatures; `getSignedTx` refuses to autofill a batch that already carries `BatchSigners`; add `verifyBatchSigners(batch)`; make `verifySignature` not return `true` with unverified `BatchSigners`/`Signers`; rewrite the `combineBatchSigners` doc (returns an unsigned blob; state the order autofill → co-sign → combine → outer sign → submit with `autofill: false`).

Part of #2 (Epic: MPT API-surface audit - fix tracking). Audit PR: https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/1. Suggested branch: `fm/xrpljs-autofill-tickets-and-batch-sequences`. Size: M.

## Findings covered

- **086** — `Client.autofill` injects the account's live `Sequence` next to a caller-supplied `TicketSequence`, and `validate()` has no cross-field rule, so every ticketed submission through the sugar reaches rippled as `temSEQ_AND_TICKET` — [audit/086-autofill-injects-sequence-next-to-ticketsequence.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/086-autofill-injects-sequence-next-to-ticketsequence.md)
- **098** — `autofillBatchTxn` emits a ticketed inner transaction with no `Sequence` field at all; rippled rejects the whole batch at submission with `Field 'Sequence' is required but missing` — [audit/098-batch-autofill-emits-ticketed-inner-without-sequence.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/098-batch-autofill-emits-ticketed-inner-without-sequence.md)
- **087** — `autofillBatchTxn` adds `+1` to the outer account's inner `Sequence`s even when the outer `Batch` uses a ticket, so the issuer's inner transactions are off by one and the batch "succeeds" without doing anything — [audit/087-batch-autofill-off-by-one-under-ticketed-outer.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/087-batch-autofill-off-by-one-under-ticketed-outer.md)
- **100** — `autofill` shallow-copies a `Batch` and writes `Sequence`/`Fee`/`SigningPubKey` into the caller's inner transaction objects, so retrying the same Batch object reuses stale inner sequences while the outer gets a fresh one — and the retry reports `tesSUCCESS` having done nothing — [audit/100-autofill-mutates-inner-batch-transactions-stale-retry.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/100-autofill-mutates-inner-batch-transactions-stale-retry.md)
- **101** — `autofillBatchTxn` derives the outer account's inner `Sequence`s from `account_info`, ignoring a caller-supplied outer `Sequence`, so pre-assigned (pipelined) batches get inner sequences that are already in the past — [audit/101-batch-inner-sequences-ignore-caller-supplied-outer-sequence.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/101-batch-inner-sequences-ignore-caller-supplied-outer-sequence.md)
- **107** — The `maxFeeXRP` cap bypass for reserve-priced transactions looks only at the outer `TransactionType`, so a `Batch` containing an `AccountDelete` / `AMMCreate` / `VaultCreate` is capped below the fee the SDK itself computes — [audit/107-batch-fee-cap-bypass-is-outer-only.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/107-batch-fee-cap-bypass-is-outer-only.md)

## Affected files

- `packages/xrpl/src/client/index.ts`
- `packages/xrpl/src/sugar/autofill.ts`
- `packages/xrpl/test/client/autofill.test.ts`

## Proposed fix

Set `Sequence = 0` when `TicketSequence` is present (top level and `autofillBatchTxn`); `+1` for the outer account only when the outer consumes a sequence; anchor inner sequences to the outer's actual `Sequence` (run after it is settled); deep-copy `RawTransactions` so `autofill` never mutates the caller's inner objects; apply the `maxFeeXRP` cap bypass when any inner is reserve-priced (and extend `checkAccountDeleteBlockers` / `fail_hard` to inner `AccountDelete`); add a `validateBaseTransaction` rule for `TicketSequence` + non-zero `Sequence`.

Each finding file carries the concrete diff or code for its part; this issue is the PR-sized bundle.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Unit tests in `test/client/autofill.test.ts` (none exist for tickets today): ticketed top-level → `Sequence: 0`; ticketed inner → `Sequence: 0`; ticketed outer → inner sequences start at the account sequence; outer `Sequence: 800` → inner 801, 802; autofilling the same Batch object twice yields fresh inner sequences
- [ ] Integration (standalone): the ticketed lock and the ticketed Batch from findings 086/087/098 succeed and actually lock the holders; the retry scenario of finding 100 applies the unlock
- [ ] A Batch containing `AccountDelete` is fee'd like the top-level form
- [ ] `audit/mpt-issuer` scenario stays green

## Breaking?

No

- none

## Findings covered

- **062** — `waitForFinalTransactionOutcome` throws "expired" before its final `tx` lookup, so a transaction validated in its last allowed ledger is reported as failed with "Preliminary result: tesSUCCESS" — [audit/062-submitandwait-expiry-check-precedes-final-tx-lookup.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/062-submitandwait-expiry-check-precedes-final-tx-lookup.md)

- **025** — `submitAndWait` reports failure through three unrelated surfaces (`tem*` throws, `tec*` resolves, `tef*`/`ter*` time out) and ships no helper to read the engine result — [audit/025-submitandwait-three-failure-surfaces-no-result-helper.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/025-submitandwait-three-failure-surfaces-no-result-helper.md)

## Findings covered

- **070** — Odd-length hex passes every validator; the signed path drops the last nibble while `simulate`/JSON submit pads the first, so the same object yields different bytes on the wire — [audit/070-odd-length-hex-truncated-on-signed-path.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/070-odd-length-hex-truncated-on-signed-path.md)

Part of #2 (Epic: MPT API-surface audit - fix tracking). Audit PR: https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/1. Suggested branch: `fm/xrpljs-codec-mpt-amount-hardening`. Size: S.

## Findings covered

- **022** — `ripple-binary-codec` silently truncates MPT `value` strings ≥ 2^64 to their low 64 bits (2^64 + 5 encodes as 5) — [audit/022-binary-codec-silently-truncates-mpt-values-above-2-64.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/022-binary-codec-silently-truncates-mpt-values-above-2-64.md)
- **023** — `ripple-binary-codec` accepts `"0x10"`, `"+7"`, `" 9"` as MPT values (JavaScript `BigInt` semantics) and throws a raw `SyntaxError` for `"1e2"` — [audit/023-binary-codec-accepts-non-canonical-mpt-value-strings.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/023-binary-codec-accepts-non-canonical-mpt-value-strings.md)
- **096** — The codec's `UInt32.from(string)` is an unchecked `parseInt` and `UInt64.from(number | bigint)` truncates at 2^64 / loses precision above 2^53; both are reachable through `encode` and `client.submit(preSignedObject)` without `validate()` — [audit/096-codec-lenient-uint-numeric-and-string-inputs.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/096-codec-lenient-uint-numeric-and-string-inputs.md)
- **085** — The binary codec's MPT amount error fixtures are label-only (`toThrow()` with no reason) and stop at 2^64−1, so the range bug in 022 sat next to a test named "Value is too large" — [audit/085-codec-mpt-error-fixtures-assert-bare-throw.md](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/085-codec-mpt-error-fixtures-assert-bare-throw.md)

- `packages/ripple-binary-codec/src/types/amount.ts`
- `packages/ripple-binary-codec/src/types/uint-32.ts`
- `packages/ripple-binary-codec/src/types/uint-64.ts`
- `packages/ripple-binary-codec/test/amount.test.ts`
- `packages/ripple-binary-codec/test/fixtures/data-driven-tests.json`

## Proposed fix

`assertMptIsValid`: `/^(0|[1-9][0-9]*)$/` and `BigInt(v) <= 2^63-1` (closes the bit-63-only check that lets 2^64+5 encode as 5, and the `0x`/`+`/whitespace/`1e2` leniency); `UInt32.from(string)` strict decimal + range; `UInt64.from(number|bigint)` safe-integer/range checks; `amount.test.ts` asserts the fixture's error text; add vectors 2^64, 2^64+5, 2^65 and the non-canonical strings. Decide deliberately about `0x` fixtures (finding 023 note).

Each finding file carries the concrete diff or code for its part; this issue is the PR-sized bundle.

body:
## Summary

An adversarial audit of the `xrpl` package's Multi-Purpose Token (MPT) API surface, driven by a runnable compliance-token issuer (clawback, allow-listing, per-holder and global lock, permissioned-domain admission) run against a local standalone rippled 3.4.0-rc1 with this checkout's build. Seven rounds (one build round, then adversarial sweeps re-verified on the ledger or against the built package) produced **107 findings**: two blockers that put a different transaction on the wire than the developer wrote with no error from any layer (a codec range check, and lowercase field names silently dropped when signing so a per-holder lock becomes a global freeze), a `submitAndWait` that can report a validated transaction as expired, balance helpers that do not know MPTs exist, a ticket/Batch path that is broken at every level, and a long tail of type, validator, RPC-shape and documentation gaps. This epic tracks the fixes; each work-breakdown unit below is one branch and one PR that can be implemented, tested and reviewed independently. No library code is changed by the audit PR itself.

- Audit PR: https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/pull/1
- Report: [`audit/README.md`](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/README.md) · findings: [`audit/001`–`audit/107`](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/tree/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit) · plan: [`audit/PLAN.md`](https://github.com/theahaco/xrpl.js/blob/fm/xrpljs-mpt-audit-x1/audit/PLAN.md)
- Executable evidence: `audit/mpt-issuer` (`npm run scenario` 63/63; `npm run type-repros` compiles only while the type findings exist; `npm run probes` compares `validate()` with rippled `simulate`)

## Severity tally

| blocker | major | minor | paper-cut | total |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 2 | 24 | 60 | 21 | 107 |

## Requirement mapping

| Requirement | Ledger mechanism | Achievable as stated? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Clawback | `tfMPTCanClawback` + `Clawback { Amount: { mpt_issuance_id, value }, Holder }` | Yes. Works while the holder is locked, unauthorized and during a global freeze; claws back `min(value, balance)`. |
| Pre-emptive ban | `tfMPTRequireAuth` allow-listing; nothing can be written on-ledger for an address that has not opted in (`tecOBJECT_NOT_FOUND`), and opt-in cannot be prevented | **Not as stated.** Closest model: off-ledger registry + never authorize + lock the empty `MPToken` the moment it appears (lock-on-arrival), and lock + claw back for current holders. rippled cannot enumerate holders (`mpt_holders` is Clio-only). Alternative: permissioned-domain admission via credentials — still not pre-emptive. See finding 028. |
| Freeze newly banned accounts | `MPTokenIssuanceSet { Holder, Flags: tfMPTLock }` | Yes, once the `MPToken` exists; lock beats a later authorization; issuer↔holder payments remain allowed; a locked holder can never delete its entry. |
| Global freeze | `MPTokenIssuanceSet { Flags: tfMPTLock }` / `tfMPTUnlock` | Yes; holder↔holder payments fail `tecLOCKED`, issuer-direction payments still succeed; idempotent; per-holder locks survive a global unlock. |
